name: Residence Permit for the Purpose of Family Reunification

requirements.blocker_text: Eligible sponsors: holders of a residence permit (EXCLUDING seasonal-employment, investment-related-work, standard-employment, White Card, or study/training/traineeship/volunteer-service permits), holders of immigration/settlement permits or permanent residence cards, Hungarian citizens, recognised refugees (if the marriage predates entry to Hungary), and parents of unaccompanied minors with refugee status. Guest self-employment permit holders must have held that status for at least 1 year before sponsoring.

Eligible relatives: spouses (including registered partners); minor children (biological, adopted, or foster); dependent minor children under the applicant's parental custody; and persons with parental custody of a minor Hungarian-citizen child in the same household.
Requires a certificate from a credit institution demonstrating sufficient financial means (no fixed minimum amount published).

evidence_required.document: Birth, marriage, or adoption certificate proving the relationship

outcome.duration_length: tied to the sponsor's own residence permit validity

sources.title: National Directorate-General for Aliens Policing (OIF) -- Residence Permit for the Purpose of Family Reunification: eligible relatives, sponsor eligibility and exclusions, 21/70-day processing

notes: NEW ROUTE, part of Hungary's initial build. Confirmed directly at tier-1. Standard processing: 21 days; 70 days when combined with an employment application. UNUSUALLY LONG SPONSOR-EXCLUSION LIST confirmed at tier-1: holders of standard-employment permits (hu_work_sponsored_employment), White Card (hu_white_card), seasonal-employment, and investment-related-work permits CANNOT sponsor family reunification at all -- a materially more restrictive design than most other countries in this dataset, where the main employment route typically does confer family-sponsorship rights. 'Investment-related work' is not further defined in the source; out of caution this is treated as potentially covering hu_guest_investor, which is therefore excluded from required_prior_route_ids pending clearer confirmation. work_rights for the reunified family member set to 'restricted' as a conservative placeholder -- the tier-1 page did not specify the work-rights regime for admitted family members.
